description: Define scoring and score presentation against the approved mockups in .lore/work/mockups/Golden City Rhythm Concert.webp and Neon Twilight Rhythm City.webp. design:
Approved scoring direction (2026-10-16 discussion; not yet implemented)

Score measures timing accuracy and sustained successful hits. It is separate from Renown, Personal Strength, Twilight Strength, and victory. Any future connection to those systems is deferred.

BASE POINTS
- Perfect: 100 base points throughout the Perfect timing window.
- Good: base points fall linearly from 100 at the Perfect boundary to 0 at the Miss boundary, based on absolute timing error. With error e, Perfect boundary P and Miss boundary G: 100 * (G - e) / (G - P) for P < e < G.
- Miss: 0 points and resets the combo.
- Both Perfect and Good advance the successful-hit streak.

COMBO
- Notes 1-10 of a successful streak: x1; 11-20: x2; 21-30: x3; 31-40: x4; 41 onward: x5.
- The tenth successful hit earns the next multiplier for the following note, not retroactively for itself. Cap at x5.
- Multiply each hit’s base points by its current multiplier.
- A 60-note all-Perfect performance scores 1,000 + 2,000 + 3,000 + 4,000 + 10,000 = 20,000 points.

STARS
- Each song uses its theoretical all-Perfect Normal-difficulty maximum score, including combo multipliers, as a shared baseline across difficulties.
- Five visible stars progressively fill as normal stars, then progressively turn gold: two successive progress tracks using the same five stars, not ten separate icons.
- Normal-star thresholds: 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60% of the baseline.
- Gold-star thresholds: 70%, 75%, 80%, 85%, 90% of the baseline.
- Scores may exceed the Normal baseline; the star display caps at five gold stars.
- Consistent rules matter, not enforced difficulty-specific ceilings. Easy may earn gold, including five gold, if it reaches the shared thresholds. No artificial difficulty restriction or chart rebalance is required to prevent this.

MODES
- Score and combo continue uninterrupted through Audience, Twilight, and Radiant, including the remaining song after Twilight defeat.
- Mode changes and Twilight defeat do not reset the combo or stop scoring. Radiant freezes strength changes, not score accumulation.


SCORE REPRESENTATION AND TIMING
- The score itself must be integer-valued, not merely displayed as an integer over a fractional accumulated score.
- Start with the existing gameplay timing boundaries. Separate scoring-specific timing windows may be considered later; they are not decided or required now.
- The precise per-hit integer rounding convention has not been selected; do not present one as user-approved.

PRESENTATION
- Follow the approved mockups, adjusted to show five stars with the fill-then-gold behavior above.
- Show the current multiplier as part of the combo area.

SCOPE
- These rules and presentation direction are documented design decisions, not implemented functionality.
- Persistence, leaderboards, unlocks, meta-progression, and future connections between score and strength are separate future work, not blockers for this scoring system.
- No replacement visual direction or implementation is authorized by this documentation update.
